priorStories.headline: Huawei convicted of fraud and trade-secret conspiracy
priorStories.body:
A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Huawei on 10 criminal counts, including bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. The Justice Department said Huawei and three subsidiaries were convicted of offenses involving Iran sanctions, fraud and money laundering.

Jurors acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy. Sentencing remains pending, and a company attorney said Huawei would appeal the convictions.

sources.name: US Department of Justice via Forth

candidates.summary: Colombian security forces stormed a supermarket in Cartagena early November 25, ending a hostage siege that began the preceding day. President Abelardo de la Espriella said all remaining hostages were rescued and one captor was killed.
candidates.title: Colombian forces end Cartagena supermarket hostage siege

candidates.summary: Rescuers recovered three bodies on November 25 from an unauthorized gold mine in Bogor, West Java, and searched for 23 other miners believed trapped, AP reported. The flooding occurred late November 23 when heavy rain caused a nearby river to overflow into the shaft. Indonesia's search-and-rescue agency said the bodies were recovered shortly after midday local time; high water, narrow access and limited lighting complicated operations.
candidates.title: Three bodies recovered from flooded Indonesian gold mine

candidates.summary: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act on November 25, alongside an equity-financing fund that Reuters reported at €50 billion. The package seeks to strengthen European quantum technology and favour EU-controlled suppliers in relevant procurement, with exceptions for reciprocal partners. The legislation remains a proposal requiring negotiations with EU member countries and the European Parliament before it can become law.
candidates.title: European Commission proposes Quantum Act and technology equity fund

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Economic Analysis released its second estimate of third-quarter GDP on November 25, revising annualized real growth to 4.3% from 3.4%. The revision primarily reflected higher estimates of investment and consumer spending. Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized rate in the second quarter.
candidates.title: US third-quarter GDP growth revised to 4.3% annualized

candidates.summary: The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported on November 25 that October's personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier and 0.3% from September. Excluding food and energy, prices increased 3.3% annually and 0.3% monthly. Personal income rose 0.7%, nominal consumer spending increased 0.3%, and inflation-adjusted spending was essentially unchanged. The personal saving rate was 4.1%.
candidates.title: October US PCE inflation reaches 3.8% year over year

candidates.summary: The US Army detonated roughly five tons of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on November 25. Officials said degradation made moving or opening the stored material unsafe. Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe said initial analysis supplied by federal partners and Iowa emergency officials indicated that mitigation measures appeared successful and the explosion was well-contained; monitoring continued.
candidates.title: Army detonates unstable lead azide stockpile in Iowa

candidates.summary: Rescuers recovered nine bodies by November 25 evening local time from flooded unauthorized gold-mine shafts in Bogor, West Java, up from three reported earlier, AP reported. Seventeen other miners were believed trapped. Flooding began late November 23 after heavy rain caused the nearby Ciseureuh River to overflow. Search officials said high water, narrow access, slippery terrain and limited lighting complicated the operation.
candidates.title: Death toll at flooded Indonesian gold mine rises to nine

candidates.summary: Macy’s announced on November 25 that its Thanksgiving Day Parade would move from November 26 to November 28 because of expected severe weather in New York City. The company said the decision followed consultation with city and agency partners and prioritized participant and spectator safety. Organizers said operational details were still being finalized.
candidates.title: Macy’s postpones Thanksgiving parade because of expected severe weather
candidates.geography: New York City, New York, United States

candidates.summary: US District Judge Christopher Cooper issued a preliminary injunction on November 25 blocking enforcement of President Donald Trump’s August executive order restricting birthright citizenship against children covered by a class action. A Maryland judge had separately blocked the order in September. The administration would need to overturn both decisions before enforcing it. The White House criticized Cooper’s decision and defended the order.
candidates.title: Second federal judge blocks Trump’s revised birthright citizenship order

candidates.summary: Judges in Benjamin Netanyahu’s corruption trial recommended on November 25 that prosecutors drop Case 4000, which alleges regulatory favors for favorable news coverage, and reconsider Case 2000. The court explicitly said the recommendation was not a ruling. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said she would review the statements with prosecutors. Netanyahu denies wrongdoing and has pleaded not guilty.
candidates.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping one Netanyahu corruption case

candidates.summary: A vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on Greater Cairo’s Ring Road on November 25, killing 31 people and injuring 21, Egyptian authorities said. Prosecutors said preliminary assessments found 27 vehicles charred near a tunnel in Giza’s Al-Warraq district. Authorities ordered DNA sampling to identify victims, and casualty and damage assessments continued.
candidates.title: Fuel tanker fire on Cairo ring road kills 31

candidates.summary: The CDC’s November 25 measles update reported 6,039 confirmed US cases through November 24, including 18 among international visitors. The federal death tally rose to nine after additional state reports were verified, an HHS spokesperson told Reuters. Reuters counted at least 14 measles-associated deaths in publicly reported state figures, noting that federal and state totals use different reporting processes. The CDC said its death count could change as reviews continued.
candidates.title: CDC reports 6,039 measles cases and nine verified deaths in 2026

sources.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

candidates.summary: Brazil’s central bank and National Monetary Council announced measures on November 25 to limit risks from household indebtedness. They include restrictions on additional unsecured lending to certain borrowers with overdue debt and gradual credit-card limit reductions for customers repeatedly using revolving credit after incomplete payments. Financial institutions must also strengthen monitoring of excessive indebtedness. Most provisions are scheduled to take effect July 1, 2027, rather than immediately.
candidates.title: Brazil announces lending safeguards to address household indebtedness

candidates.summary: The Federal Reserve’s November 25 Beige Book reported slight-to-moderate economic growth in eight districts and no change in four. Employment rose slightly overall, while prices increased moderately and businesses reported persistent energy, transportation, healthcare, insurance and tariff-related costs. Consumer spending was little changed. The report summarized outside contacts’ observations collected on or before November 16; it was not a statement of Federal Reserve officials’ views.
candidates.title: Fed Beige Book reports continued growth and persistent cost pressures

candidates.summary: The US Army detonated roughly five tons of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on November 25. At a news conference two hours later, Maj. Gen. Eric Shirley said all the material had been destroyed, with no secondary explosions or infrastructure damage. The EPA said its real-time monitors had detected no airborne lead more than an hour after the blast. These were initial monitoring findings, not a final environmental assessment.
candidates.title: Army reports Iowa lead azide destruction successful; initial monitors detect no airborne lead
